newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to privatise 7 state banks - govt official.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to privatise 7 state banks - govt official.

text.p: Bulgaria's socialist government plans to privatise all state-owned banks except Bulbank (Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) in the coming months, a government official told Reuters on Thursday.
"The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) is open to all offers of serious investors that have an interest in buying Bulgarian banks," BCC executive director Valentin Tsvetanov said.
The BCC manages state equity in domestic commercial banks.
Only Bulbank, Bulgaria's most stable bank, will remain state-owned under the government's plans, he added.
"Bulbank is the only institution representing Bulgaria in the international financial community," Tsvetanov said.

He declined to give further details on the sell-off plans but said they included Balkanbank and Economic Bank, which were on an unofficial list of banks slated for closure or special supervision that has recently circulated in local media.
The other five banks expected to be sold are Biohim Bank, Bulgarian Post Bank, Hebros Bank, Express Bank and United Bulgarian Bank.
Economic Bank has the largest share of debts to foreign creditors among the seven, amounting to around $150 million.
The seven banks, several of which are suffering severe liquidity problems, were recapitalised three months ago with dollar-denominated government securities at a total cost of $400 million.

All the banks had a negative capital to assets ratio before the government conducted the recapitalisation operation, which was part of a funding agreement clinched with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in July.
The banks' shares will not be offered publicly as the government is keen to attract strong foreign investors, Tsvetanov said.
"So far we have not discussed the possible sell-off of Mineralbank," Tsvetanov added, referring to the state-owned institution that the central bank is currently trying to shut.
The Sofia city court is expected to rule on the insolvency suit against Mineralbank on September 25.
Commenting on the chances of selling state banks to serious foreign investors, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov earlier on Thursday sounded a cautious note.
"Garbage should be thrown away, not sold," he told reporters.
